title: Boy in da Corner
label: XL Recordings
format: Album (LP/CD; formats not itemised in sources opened)

type.basis: Album: holds several specimens. Multi-track items are not coded as a single genotype.

sound.text: Dizzee says none of the album's tracks is at 140 bpm; the 140 bpm norm came later.
Tracks usually started from drums; samples were spread across a keyboard, one per key; no MPC used.
Entertainment Weekly (via Wikipedia): UK garage beats combined with a distinctly British sensibility; Pitchfork praised its 'cutting sonics'.
Rock edge attributed by Dizzee to grunge and Black Sabbath influences ('Stop Dat').

context.text: Won the 2003 Mercury Prize; peaked at no. 23 on the UK Albums Chart; later certified platinum (BPI, 2018).
Complex (B.J. Steiner) credits it with bringing grime to the rest of the world.
Ranked no. 4 in FACT's 'The 20 best Grime records ever made'.
Made in about a year, when Dizzee was largely unknown outside London pirate radio; he was 18 at release.
